correctness.rationale: For an n-gon the support function of P-P is a regular N-gon with N=n if n even, 2n if n odd. Centering phase at a difference-body width maximum gives f_N(theta)=(h_N/sin h_N) cos d_N(theta), h_N=pi/N, mean 1. Its Fourier coefficient at kN equals (-1)^(k+1)/(k^2N^2-1). Haar covariance retains exactly kN=lM=j lcm(N,M), yielding the arithmetic parity shift by (r+s)pi/L. The autocorrelation K_L is rigorously strictly decreasing on (0,pi/L): its derivative is [t sin(2h-t)-(2h-t)sin t]/(4h), negative by strict decrease of sin(x)/x for 0<x<2h<=pi/2. This proves global unique extrema (not only local stationary phases), with strict positivity of Minkowski weights transferring to variance and coefficient of variation. Closed forms for the two extrema follow from cell integration and yield L^-4 coefficients. I independently computed twelve direct vertex-width covariances for polygon pairs (3,4),(4,8),(4,6),(5,9) and three angles each, within 2e-9 of Fourier law. All integer n,m>=3 and arbitrary positive radii/weights are covered analytically.

value.rationale: The simultaneous directional-width fluctuation of two regular polygons is a natural geometric statistic, and positive Minkowski combination leads to a meaningful orientation design problem. Its global optimizer and equality cases collapsing to one LCM and parity bit, including counterintuitive square-octagon alignment, are exact structural information not provided by routine individual width-variance tables. The problem is self-contained and naturally generalizes classical width deviation.

limitations: Classical width Fourier methods underlie the proof; no claim to invent covariance calculability.
Only positive two-factor weights and common Haar view directions, not arbitrary polygons or three-plus factors.
